title: A DELEGATION FROM BASTAR MANDAL CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau President's Secretariat A DELEGATION FROM BASTAR MANDAL CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT WITH THE GOVERNMENT'S EFFORTS AND THE ACTIVE PARTICIPATION OF THE PEOPLE OF BASTAR, THE REGION IS MOVING ON THE PATH OF DEVELOPMENT: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi A delegation from Bastar Mandal comprising winners of Bastar Pandum 2026, Pargana Manjhi and Chalaki of Bastar called on the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre today (July 30, 2026). Among the dignitaries present on the occasion were Union Minister for Home Affairs and Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah and Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Shri Vishnu Deo Sai. Addressing the gathering, the President said that the Bastar Pandum is not merely a cultural event; it is a celebration of Bastar's glorious traditions and cultural identity. Its objective is to establish Bastar's true identity on both national and international platforms. She underlined that events like Bastar Pandum have played a vital role in reconnecting the youth with their traditions, customs, and cultural heritage. Such events also promote tourism and create employment opportunities. The President appreciated the role of Manjhi and Chalki in preserving social life and cultural values. She said that they are an effective bridge between the community and the administration. She expressed confidence that through their dedication and leadership, they will continue to work towards happiness, peace, and prosperity in society. The President was happy to note that with the government's efforts and the active participation of the people of Bastar, the region is moving towards a new path of development. She said that people are coming out of the environment of violence and embracing new opportunities for education, employment, and development. This transformation is a sign of bright future for Bastar. Amenities such as roads, electricity, and drinking water are reaching even the remotest villages. Schools that had remained closed for long time are once again bustling with children, and the light of education is reaching every household. Today, an atmosphere of hope, trust, and progress is taking shape in Bastar. This transformation is a source of joy and pride for the entire nation. The President said that tribal youth are showcasing their talents in various fields such as education, science, art, and sports. Tribal people have an innate talent in sports and art. She was happy to note that the Bastar Olympics was recently organised in Chhattisgarh. The President expressed confidence that tribal people will participate in the developmental journey and contribute to nation building while preserving and promoting their cultural identity. She said that it is our duty to strengthen the culture of cooperation and harmony. She underlined the need to work for empowerment of women, children, deprived sections of society and senior citizens. She urged people to make conservation of water, environment and natural resources an integral part of their lives. **** MJPS/SS/PRK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291933) आगंतुक पटल  : 163 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी President's Secretariat A DELEGATION FROM BASTAR MANDAL CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT WITH THE GOVERNMENT'S EFFORTS AND THE ACTIVE PARTICIPATION OF THE PEOPLE OF BASTAR, THE REGION IS MOVING ON THE PATH OF DEVELOPMENT: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PM chairs CCS Meeting to review the situation in context of ongoing West Asia Conflict
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Prime Minister's Office PM chairs CCS Meeting to review the situation in context of ongoing West Asia Conflict PM calls for a unified and coordinated mechanism for regular monitoring of all developments to ensure expeditious implementation of measures safeguarding citizens' interests PM asks to establish a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families Requirement for fertilizers for the ensuing Rabi season assessed; PM says that all measures be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilizers PM says all efforts must be made to safeguard citizens as well as the Indian Diaspora from the impact of this conflict PM emphasises usage of renewable energy sources Cabinet Secretary briefs about initiatives taken to ensure adequate supply of petroleum products Posted On:
                30 JUL 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today chaired a meeting of the Cabinet Committee on Security (CSS) to review the situation in the context of ongoing West Asia conflict and measures taken by various Ministries and Departments. This was the 4th special CCS meeting on the issue. Cabinet Secretary briefed the CCS about the present geo-political situation. He spoke about the initiatives taken to ensure adequate supply of petroleum products, including LNG/LPG and fertilizers. He said that sources for procurement of LPG have already been diversified and the overall stock and supply position of major petroleum products remain adequate. Availability of adequate crude oil has enabled Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) refineries to operate at utilisation levels exceeding 100%, ensuring continued production of petrol, diesel and other petroleum products. Initiatives have also been taken to expand Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connections which have resulted in substantial increase in PNG connections. The Government is also facilitating industrial substitution of LPG through expansion of the National Gas Grid, augmentation of LNG import and regasification infrastructure, expansion of City Gas Distribution networks, and time-bound pipeline and last-mile connectivity approvals under the Pipeline Infrastructure Order, 2026. During the meeting, requirements for the fertilizers for the ensuing Rabi season was assessed and alternate sources of fertilizers were also discussed. Prime Minister said that all measures be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilizers. The situation of Seafarers serving on domestic as well as foreign-flagged vessels in conflict zones was also deliberated. Prime Minister directed to establish a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families. Prime Minister said that all efforts must be made to safeguard the citizens as well as the Indian Diaspora from the impact of this conflict. Prime Minister said that in order to ensure energy independence, emphasis should be made on renewable energy sources including solar energy and other non-fossil-fuel based sources. Prime Minister said that a whole of government approach be continued to be adopted to tackle the challenges arising due to the crisis. He said that a unified coordinated mechanism be put in place for regular monitoring of all the developments to ensure expeditious implementation of appropriate measures to safeguard the interests of the citizens. **** MJPS/SS/ST (Release ID: 2291992) Visitor Counter : 911 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , हिन्दी , Gujarati Prime Minister's Office PM chairs CCS Meeting to review the situation in context of ongoing West Asia Conflict PM calls for a unified and coordinated mechanism for regular monitoring of all developments to ensure expeditious implementation of measures safeguarding citizens' interests PM asks to establish a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers and their families Requirement for fertilizers for the ensuing Rabi season assessed; PM says that all measures be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilizers PM says all efforts must be made to safeguard citizens as well as the Indian Diaspora from the impact of this conflict PM emphasises usage of renewable energy sources Cabinet Secretary briefs about initiatives taken to ensure adequate supply of petroleum products Posted On:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: GLOBAL COMPETITIVENESS OF INDIA’S SPACE PROGRAMME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: GLOBAL COMPETITIVENESS OF INDIA’S SPACE PROGRAMME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi The total budget allocated to the Department of Space since 2021, year-wise, indicating the share of India's GDP and the share in the Union Budget is as given below: (Rs. in crores) Year Budget Allocated to Dept. % share of Department Budget in Union Budget % Share of Department Expenditure in India's GDP 2025-26 13416.20 0.26 0.03 2024-25 13042.75 0.27 0.04 2023-24 12543.91 0.28 0.04 2022-23 13700.00 0.35 0.04 2021-22 13949.09 0.40 0.05 Details of expenditure incurred under various schemes/ verticals are given below: Name of Scheme Nature of Expenditure Total expenditure in ₹ Crore 2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 (RE) 2026-27 (BE) Space Technology Exp. on building of Launch Vehicles, EO Satellites, Navigation, Technology demonstration satellites and creation of facilities 8873.62 7646.72 8083.43 8840.72 9601.98 10397.06 Space Applications Exp. on Applications Programmes such as NNRMS, DMS etc. 1203.62 1268.56 1475.43 1562.91 1596.27 1725.06 Space Sciences Exp. on Planetary Missions, Sponsered Research etc. 190.36 114.13 109.51 107.93 184.62 569.76 Indian National Satellite System Exp. on building of Communication Satellites 344.97 414.18 234.74 176.13 205.95 130.93 Department has carried out an assessment of India’s global standing in the space sector w.r.t the launch capability, satellite manufacturing, reusable launch technologies, human spaceflight, deep space exploration, commercial launch services, patents, research and technological innovation. Summary is given below: Launch capability: India achieved the landmark of 100 launches from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota and has established itself as a globally reliable launch service provider through PSLV, GSLV and LVM3, including dedicated commercial missions for domestic and international customers. Satellite manufacturing and launch services: India successfully launched the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission on GSLV, launched the heaviest satellite to GTO (CMS-03) from Indian soil using LVM3, and subsequently launched the heaviest commercial satellite from India for a US customer. Reusable launch technologies and future launch systems : ISRO is advancing Reusable Launch Vehicle (RLV) technologies, stage recovery, semi-cryogenic propulsion, Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV), and LOX-methane propulsion systems to enhance affordability and global competitiveness. Human spaceflight : Through the Gaganyaan Programme, India is progressing towards becoming a human spaceflight nation, supported by development of human-rated launch systems, crew module technologies and future Bharatiya Antariksh Station under Space Vision 2047. Deep space exploration: India became the first country to successfully achieve a soft landing near the lunar south pole through Chandrayaan-3 and became the third country to place a solar observatory at the Sun-Earth L1 point through the Aditya-L1 mission. Advanced space technologies : India became the fourth country to demonstrate autonomous docking and undocking in space through the SPADEX mission, an important capability for future space stations, human spaceflight and deep-space exploration. Research, innovation and technology : ISRO continues to pursue advanced R&D in reusable launch systems, space robotics, electric propulsion, quantum communication, docking technologies, planetary exploration and next-generation satellite systems, while strengthening indigenous technology development and intellectual property generation. Commercial launch services and space sector reforms: Government reforms have opened the space sector to private participation through IN-SPACe and NSIL, enabling commercialization of launch services, technology transfers, and enhanced global market participation. Indian space start-ups have achieved significant milestones, including Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S, India's first privately developed rocket launch to orbit Vikram-1; Agnikul Cosmos' Agnibaan SOrTeD mission, featuring a single-piece 3D-printed engine; and Pixxel's deployment of high-resolution hyperspectral satellite constellations, strengthening India's global presence in commercial space technologies. Through sustained achievements in launch capability, satellite development, scientific missions, commercial launches, private sector participation and advanced technology development, India has emerged as one of the world's leading spacefaring nations with a strong and expanding presence in the global space sector. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. **** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291825) आगंतुक पटल  : 232 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: GLOBAL COMPETITIVENESS OF INDIA’S SPACE PROGRAMME प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT AND INDIGENOUS SPACE TECHNOLOGY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Space PARLIAMENT QUESTION: HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT AND INDIGENOUS SPACE TECHNOLOGY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi The Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) is planned as India's first indigenous space station comprising of five modules, targeted to be established by 2035. In October,2024, Union Cabinet approved development and launch of 1 st module of BAS (BAS-01) by 2028 as part of revision in scope of Gaganyaan Programme. Baseline Design Review and System Engineering of BAS-01 completed and 31 Nos of baseline design documents released. Expert committee review completed. Design of subsystems have commenced. As part of Gaganyaan programme, new developments in the area of Human Rated Launch Vehicle (HLVM3), Orbital Module, Crew Escape System, ground infrastructure establishments, establishment of flight operations and communication network, Crew recovery operations have been carried out. Pre cursor missions TV-D1, IADT-01 and 02 have been accomplished. Activities are in advance stages for 1 st Uncrewed mission, G1. Docking systems have been worked out including electrical and mechanical interfaces. The concept demo model of Refuelling mechanism has been successfully demonstrated. Other critical technologies for human spaceflight requirement include flight suit, view port and crew seat. For Gaganyaan missions these have been currently sourced from external parties. Major critical technologies for human space programme have been identified including flight suit, view port, crew seat and docking technology. Govt of India has approved the indigenous development of these critical technologies.  Design and development of proto hardware is in progress. These initiatives will establish the technological foundation for indigenous design and development of the remaining four modules of BAS. It will build self-reliance in critical human spaceflight technologies, thereby fostering innovation and high-technology manufacturing required for human space flight. title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY IN MEDICAL AND AGRICULTURAL SECTORS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NUCLEAR TECHNOLOGY IN MEDICAL AND AGRICULTURAL SECTORS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) is advancing the peaceful applications of nuclear technology in the medical and agricultural sectors. Nuclear technology in Medical Sector: In medical sector, nuclear medicine and radioisotopes are extensively used for diagnostic and therapeutic applications, especially in cancer care. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) a constituent Unit of DAE, regularly produces radioisotopes and ready-to-use radiopharmaceuticals, which are supplied through Board of Radiation & Isotope Technology (BRIT) an industrial sector of DAE, to nuclear medicine centres across India, thereby supporting timely availability for diagnostic and therapeutic applications. DAE has taken significant efforts towards indigenous development of radiopharmaceuticals and allied products, with the objective of providing cost-effective alternatives to imported radiopharmaceuticals. Radioisotopes are indigenously produced through research reactors and cyclotrons. Radioisotopes such as Ruthenium-106, Caesium-137, and Strontium-90 milked into Yttrium-90, are recovered through the reprocessing of high-level liquid waste (HLLW). DAE is also contributing to the field of nuclear medicine through its clinical patient services units at the Radiation Medicine Centre (RMC), Mumbai, and the Radiation Medicine Research Centre (RMRC), Kolkata, which provide diagnostic and therapeutic services for cancer treatment. RMRC, Kolkata is a state-of-the-art nuclear medicine facility established in the Eastern Region under the aegis of BARC, Mumbai. The Centre has been operational since January 2024 and provides advanced and affordable diagnostic and therapeutic nuclear medicine services to patients from the Eastern and North-Eastern regions of India. Over the past several years, DAE has developed several key nuclear medicine ligands and targeted therapeutics as part of the national effort to combat cancer, especially in the areas of advanced treatment and research. DAE has developed peptide-based ligand, PSMA-617 for use in prostate cancer therapy. The in-house developed nuclear medicine ligand 177Lu-PSMA-617 is regularly supplied through BRIT to hospitals across India. Recently, DAE has developed another nuclear medicine ligand, PSMA-11, as an import substitute for production of 68Ga-PSMA11, which is used in the diagnosis of prostate cancer. Radioactive Pharmaceuticals such as Ga68 DOTANOC, Ga68 FAPI, 18F FDG are used for evaluation of various cancers such as prostate cancer, Neuroendocrine Tumors, Mucinous, Signet GI cancers, carcinoma lung, carcinoma oesophagus, breast cancer, lymphoma, etc. DAE manufactures and supplies approximately 18 different types of cold kits for the preparation of Technetium-99m radiopharmaceuticals, which are widely used for early diagnosis of diseases affecting nearly all major organs of the body, including various types of cancers. These kits enable the formulation of high-quality diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals based that play a key role in the early detection, staging, and monitoring of a broad spectrum of diseases in nuclear medicine. DAE has also developed a synthesis protocol for affordable, sesta-MIBI, which is regularly used as 99mTc-MIBI for cardiac imaging. A list of radioisotopes and radiopharmaceutical products made available in India since 2014, along with their clinical applications, is given below: DAE-RPC APPROVED RADIOPHARMACEUTICALS AND ALLIED PRODUCTS Sl. No. Name Application 1 99m Tc-Hynic-TOC Neuroendocrine tumor imaging 2 99m Tc-Hynic-TATE Neuroendocrine tumor imaging 3 99m Tc-HSA-Nanocolloid Detection of sentinel nodes in breast and other cancers 4 99m Tc-UBI (29-41) Infection imaging 5 99m Tc-HYNIC-[cyclo(RGDfk)]2 Malignant tumor imaging 6 99m Tc-TRODAT Diagnostic imaging of Parkinson’s disease 7 68 Ga-DOTA-TOC Neuroendocrine tumor imaging 8 68 Ga-PSMA-11 Prostate cancer imaging 9 [ 64 Cu]CuCl2 Produced by (n,γ) route Cancer imaging 10 [ 64 Cu]CuCl2 (No-carrier-added) Cancer imaging & 64 Cu-radiopharmaceutical preparation 11 177 Lu-DOTA-TATE Neuroendocrine cancer therapy 12 177 Lu-DOTA-NOC Neuroendocrine cancer therapy 13 177 Lu-EDTMP Bone pain palliation 14 177 Lu-Hydroxyapatite Radiation synovectomy 15 177 Lu-PSMA-617 Prostate cancer therapy 16 177 Lu-DOTMP Bone pain palliation 17 177 Lu-CHX-A-DTPA-Rituximab Therapy Lymphoma of Non-Hodgkin’s 18 177 Lu-DOTA-Rituximab Therapy Lymphoma of Non-Hodgkin’s 19 177 Lu-DOTA-Trastuzumab Breast cancer therapy 20 131 I-Lipiodol Liver cancer therapy 21 188 Re-HEDP Bone pain palliation 22 188 Re-DEDC-Lipiodol Liver cancer therapy 23 90 Y-DOTA-TATE Neuroendocrine cancer therapy 24 90 Y-Glass microsphere (BhabhaSphere) Treatment of liver cancer 25 90 Y-Hydroxyapatite Radiation synovectomy 26 166 Ho-labeled resin microspheres Liver cancer therapy Nuclear technology in Agriculture Sector: In agriculture, DAE has developed 72 improved crop varieties using radiation-induced mutagenesis along with cross breeding, which have been released and notified for commercial cultivation across the country in collaboration with ICAR and State Agricultural Universities. These varieties include rice, mustard, sesame, groundnut, uradbean, mungbean, pigeonpea, sorghum, cowpea, wheat, soybean, sunflower, banana, linseed and jute. Some of the desirable traits in these crops include higher yield, seed size, and quality traits, early maturity, climate resilient traits like drought, heat, salinity tolerance and resistance to diseases. Several of these varieties have high patronage from the farming community and are extensively grown in the country. DAE is promoting the use of radiation technologies for preservation of food and agricultural products by developing standard operating procedures (SOPs) for irradiation of agricultural commodities, preparing standards and guidelines for food irradiation, developing improved radiation facilities, and transferring radiation-based food preservation technologies to private entrepreneurs for commercialisation. Radiation processing extends the shelf life of perishable produce, reduces post-harvest losses, enables chemical-free preservation of grains and spices, and helps meet international phytosanitary requirements for export. Currently, till date 42 food irradiation facilities have been commissioned in the country, including in the Government sector and in the private sector. Cobalt 60 (Co-60) based irradiators are used for sterilisation of medical products and self-life extension of agriculture & marine products. DAE is also contributing to the field of nuclear medicine through its clinical patient services units at the Radiation Medicine Centre (RMC), Mumbai, and the Radiation Medicine Research Centre (RMRC), Kolkata, which provide diagnostic and therapeutic services for cancer treatment. RMRC, Kolkata is a state-of-the-art nuclear medicine facility established in the Eastern Region under the aegis of BARC, Mumbai. The Centre has been operational since January 2024 and provides advanced and affordable diagnostic and therapeutic nuclear medicine services to patients from the Eastern and North-Eastern regions of India. title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ENHANCING NUCLEAR ENERGY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: ENHANCING NUCLEAR ENERGY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi The Government has drawn up a roadmap for reaching the 100 GW nuclear power capacity in the next two decades i.e. by 2047, as announced in the Nuclear Energy Mission in the Union Budget 2025-26, thereby increasing the share of reliable, low-carbon base-load nuclear energy in the country's energy mix and supporting the vision of Viksit Bharat and the goal of Net Zero carbon emissions by 2070. The roadmap follows a two-pronged strategy comprising deployment of indigenous 700 MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) and large imported advanced reactors at greenfield sites, along with the development and deployment of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) for brownfield applications such as repurposing retiring fossil fuel power plants, captive power for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications. As per the roadmap, the present nuclear power capacity of 8.78 GW is expected to reach about 22 GW by 2031-32 on progressive completion of projects presently at various stages of implementation. Another 32 GW of nuclear power capacity is envisaged to be set up beyond 2032 by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) that is a Public Sector Enterprise under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). This will comprise indigenous Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs) and Light Water Reactors (LWRs) planned to be setup by 2047, taking the NPCIL’s nuclear power capacity to about 54 GW. The balance of 46 GW comprising reactors of different technologies, is expected to be set up by other Public Sector Enterprises (Central & State), Private sector and Joint Ventures in different business models. As announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 the Government envisions development and deployment of indigenously designed Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) under the Nuclear Energy Mission, with a target to operationalise at least five indigenous SMRs by 2033. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), a constituent unit of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) has undertaken design and development of pressurised water reactor (PWR) technology based on Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) namely, 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200), 55 MWe Small Modular Reactor (SMR-55), and a High Temperature Gas Cooled Reactor (HTGCR) having capacity up to 5 MWth, which can be coupled with suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production. In view of the availability of requisite in-house expertise for advanced nuclear technology development, international collaborations for SMR technology is not envisaged. However, India, as a Member State of the IAEA, regularly participates in technical events organised by the Agency for knowledge sharing. The estimated time for construction of these SMRs is 60 to 72 months from receipt of financial approval. title: National Advisory Board on Management of Genetic Resources Charts Roadmap for Strengthening India's Agrobiodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Utilization
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare National Advisory Board on Management of Genetic Resources Charts Roadmap for Strengthening India's Agrobiodiversity Conservation and Sustainable Utilization Board calls for integrated management of plant, animal, fish, microbial and insect genetic resources to support Viksit Bharat and climate-resilient agriculture प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi Recognising the strategic importance of genetic resources for ensuring India's food, nutrition, environmental and livelihood security, the newly reconstituted ‘National Advisory Board on Management of Genetic Resources (NABMGR)’ held its first meeting on July 29, 2026 at the ICAR–National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (ICAR-NBPGR), New Delhi. The NABMGR was first constituted by the President of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) in 2011, under the chairmanship of Padma Bhushan Dr R.S. Paroda, Former Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), and Director General, ICAR. In 2026, ICAR reconstituted the Board again under the chairmanship of Dr Paroda and the co-chairmanship of Dr M.L. Jat, Secretary, DARE, and Director General, ICAR. The reconstituted Board brings together experts and key stakeholders to recommend national policies and strategies on agrobiodiversity, to promote coordinated management of plant, animal, fish, microbial, and insect genetic resources and advise on emerging national and international issues related to genetic resources. The meeting of NABMGR held on July 29, was attended by senior representatives from the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC), Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Botanical Survey of India (BSI), National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB), National Seed Association of India (NSAI), Bioversity International, Deputy Directors General of ICAR, Directors of the six ICAR National Bureaux managing genetic resources, farmer representatives and other eminent experts. In his opening remarks, Dr. Paroda observed that India's rich diversity of plant, animal, fish, microbial and insect genetic resources is a national strategic asset that underpins long-term food and nutritional security, climate resilience and sustainable agricultural development. He emphasised the need for strategic prioritisation by each National Bureau so that conservation and management efforts are closely aligned with emerging national needs. He highlighted the importance of enhancing the use of conserved germplasm, including wild relatives/species, in crop, livestock and fish improvement programmes to broaden the genetic base and accelerate the development of climate-resilient and high-performing varieties and breeds. Dr Paroda recalled the successful organisation of the first International Agrobiodiversity Congress (IAC) in 2016, inaugurated by the Hon'ble Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. He urged the effective implementation of the recommendations of the Delhi Declaration on Agrobiodiversity adopted during the Congress. He called for a review of the progress made so far and the preparation of a clear roadmap for future action. Further, he underscored the importance of strengthening international collaboration, particularly with countries in Central Asia and South-East Asia, to facilitate access to valuable genetic resources. He emphasised the need to reinforce existing Memoranda of Understanding and promote strategic exchange of germplasm, especially for crops such as cotton, rambutan, avocado, mangosteen etc. and livestock species such as sheep from these regions. The development of an appropriate legal framework to protect the rights of breeders and farmers for animal and fish genetic resources, on the lines of the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act (PPV&FRA) was also advocated by Dr Paroda. He observed that such a framework would encourage innovation while safeguarding the interests of livestock keepers and fish farmers. Dr M.L. Jat highlighted that effective management of genetic resources must be closely integrated with advances in soil science, digital agriculture and crop improvement. He stressed that identifying crop accessions best suited to specific soil types and agro-ecological regions would accelerate the development of climate-resilient and location-specific production systems. He noted that India has built a strong and unparalleled National Agricultural Research, Education and Extension System (NAREES), led by ICAR, that significantly facilitated the conservation, characterization and sustainable use of genetic resources, ensuring their availability for both present and future generations. He expressed confidence that the reconstituted NABMGR with representation from relevant Ministries, Departments and ICAR Bureaux, would strengthen inter-agency coordination and provide strategic guidance for the conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits arising from India's genetic resources. During the meeting, the Directors of the six ICAR National Bureaux presented the major achievements of their respective institutes during the period 2021–2026 and outlined their roadmaps for 2026–2031, focusing on initiatives aligned with national priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The Board deliberated on several strategic issues relating to the conservation and sustainable utilization of agricultural genetic resources. It recommended strengthening pre-breeding programmes to facilitate greater use of conserved germplasm in crop improvement, identifying unexplored regions for systematic germplasm collection during 2026–2031, and enhancing collaboration among the ICAR National Bureaux to develop an integrated national genetic resources management framework. A full-fledged inter-institutional program was recommended for mainstreaming traditional/ opportunity crop varieties/breeds/species of plants, microbes, insects, animals and fishes which was endorsed by the Padma Shri Mr Sunda Ram Verma, a progressive farmer. The Board also reviewed the status of delegation of responsibilities relating to agrobiodiversity from the National Biodiversity Authority to DARE/ICAR under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and discussed measures to strengthen the implementation of Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) provisions. Members deliberated on mainstreaming traditional and underutilised crop varieties, animal breeds, fish species, microorganisms and insects through an inter-institutional programme, and reviewed the progress made in establishing the National Safety Genebank (NSG). Chairman of NBAMGR suggested that efforts be made to complete the NSG in a timely manner so that it can be dedicated to the nation during the centenary celebrations of ICAR (2028-29) The meeting reaffirmed the Board's commitment to providing strategic policy guidance for conserving and sustainably utilizing India's invaluable genetic resources through greater scientific collaboration, institutional convergence and evidence-based decision-making. The recommendations are expected to strengthen the country's agrobiodiversity governance and contribute significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat by enhancing agricultural resilience, food security and sustainable development. ***** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291907) आगंतुक पटल  : 140 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Agriculture &

title: APEDA Facilitates First-Ever Sea Shipment of Value-Added Flavoured Makhana from Bihar to Canada
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry APEDA Facilitates First-Ever Sea Shipment of Value-Added Flavoured Makhana from Bihar to Canada Value-Added Makhana Exports Boost Farmers' Returns by Over 50%, Strengthen Bihar's Global Footprint प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India, facilitated the flag-off of the first-ever sea shipment of value-added flavoured Makhana (fox nuts) from Darbhanga, Bihar, to Canada on 29 July 2026. The milestone export marks a significant step in promoting Bihar's premium agricultural produce in global markets while expanding the state's basket of value-added agricultural exports. The consignment, comprising 7 metric tonnes packed in two containers, was dispatched through Mundra Port to ZKV Foods, Canada. The flavoured Makhana was processed and packaged by Nutrivin Agro Private Limited in accordance with international quality and food safety standards, reflecting Bihar's growing capabilities in food processing, value addition and export-oriented manufacturing. The flag-off ceremony was graced by APEDA Chairman, Shri Abhishek Dev, who appreciated the collective efforts of the exporter, processors, farmers, industry stakeholders and APEDA officials in facilitating the shipment. He said such collaborative initiatives are strengthening Bihar's agri-export ecosystem, promoting value-added agricultural products and expanding global market access for the state's unique produce. The event was attended by Dr. Manoj Kumar, Scientist, ICAR Research Complex for Eastern Region, Research Centre for Makhana, Darbhanga; Shri Loknath Thakur, District Agriculture Marketing Officer; senior officers of APEDA; and exporters and stakeholders associated with the Makhana value chain. Makhana, popularly known as fox nuts, is one of Bihar's flagship agricultural products, with the state accounting for the largest share of India's production. Renowned for its nutritional value and premium quality, Bihar's Makhana has witnessed growing demand in international markets owing to increasing consumer preference for healthy and value-added food products. The export of flavoured Makhana is expected to further diversify export opportunities while enhancing the global recognition of this unique product. The export of value-added flavoured Makhana has enabled associated Makhana farmers to realise over 50 per cent higher returns through value addition and improved access to international markets. It also demonstrates the potential of processing, branding and export-oriented value addition in enhancing the competitiveness of India's agricultural products while strengthening farmers' integration with global value chains. APEDA has been consistently working to develop Bihar as a leading agri-export hub through capacity building, export infrastructure development, quality compliance, market linkages and value addition. It continues to work closely with State Governments, exporters, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), processors and other stakeholders to strengthen India's agri-export ecosystem through quality assurance, export facilitation and market development. The export of flavoured Makhana is expected to further diversify export opportunities while enhancing the global recognition of this unique product. title: Raksha Rajya Mantri Chaired the Joint IAF – SIDM Seminar ‘SANKALP’ on Indigenisation
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence Raksha Rajya Mantri Chaired the Joint IAF – SIDM Seminar ‘SANKALP’ on Indigenisation प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:09PM by PIB Delhi Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth chaired a seminar on indigenisation themed ‘SANKALP’ , jointly organised by Indian Air Force and the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers  (SIDM), on July 30, 2026 in New Delhi. SANKALP stands for self-reliance, atmanirbhar bharat, native development,  and knowledge linked partnership. In his keynote address, RRM emphasized that the aim of indegenisation is to create a stronger defence ecosystem where innovation leads the way and ideas are transformed into useful products which further strengthen our defence capabilities. Appreciating the conduct of events like ‘SANKALP’, Shri Seth expressed his belief that the platform will provide opportunities to various stakeholders to discuss and exchange ideas on Indigenous Maintenance Repair and Overhaul (MRO), Component Manufacturing, Certification, Technology Absorption and future Aerospace Requirements. During the event, RRM also launched a book on ‘SANKALP 2026: Problem statements of Indian Air Force in the presence of Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, President SIDM Shri Arun T. Ramchandani, senior IAF officers and industry leaders. Air Marshal Sanjay Ghuratia, Air Officer-in-charge, Maintenance delivered the inaugural address. The event provided a platform for deliberations on the Indian Air Force & indigenisation priorities, sustainment requirements and technological advancements. Representatives from the Ministry of Defence, Defence Forces, Centre for Military Air Worthiness and Certification (CEMILAC), Director General of Aeronautical Quality Assurance (DGAQA), SIDM, industry and academia participated in the event. The industry partners showcased indigenous capabilities in the aero-space sector. The event concluded with focused Business-to-Business interactions between IAF representatives, industry participants, CEMILAC and DGAQA. The event underscored the shared commitment of all stakeholders for Atmanirbhar Bharat. **** VK/JS/Ruchi (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291821) आगंतुक पटल  : 251 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Defence Raksha Rajya Mantri Chaired the Joint IAF – SIDM Seminar ‘SANKALP’ on Indigenisation प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Compliance by industries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Compliance by industries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi City Specific Clean Air Action Plans have been prepared for 130 cities under National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) mainly to target air pollution sources like soil & road dust, vehicular emissions, waste burning, construction & demolition activities and greening activities. State Action Plans prepared under NCAP address industrial pollution through framing polices for use of approved fuels by industries, promotion of clean technologies, laydown city gas distribution network to promote use of cleaner fuels, switching conventional fuels to cleaner fuels (gaseous fuels (CNG/ PNG/ CBG) by industries/ commercial units, etc. Actions towards control of industrial pollution are primarily implemented by industries, while monitoring and enforcement of industrial emission and discharge norms are carried out by the CPCB and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/Pollution Control Committees (PCCs) through the Consent mechanism under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and necessary action is taken to ensure compliance with the provisions of the said Acts. As per reports submitted by Urban Local bodies (ULBs), 11,108 industries located in NCAP Cities have transitioned to cleaner fuels such as natural gas, PNG/LNG, LPG, biogas, etc. Under NCAP, air quality performance linked grant of ₹ 16,423.55 crore has been provided to 130 cities during FY 2019-20 till 2025-26 through XVth Finance Commission (XV FC) Million-Plus Cities Challenge Fund (MPCCF) (in case of 48 Million-Plus cities) and the Central Sector Scheme (CSS) ‘Control of Pollution’ (CP) of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (in case of 82 Non-Attainment cities). So far, cities have reported the utilization of Rs.11,575.54 crore (70.5%) on PRANA portal. District/ City level Implementation and Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of District Collector/ Municipal Commissioner periodically monitors the implementation of City clean air action plans under NCAP. Further, State level Steering Committee under the Chairmanship of Chief Secretary and Air Quality Monitoring Committee under the Chairmanship of Additional Chief Secretary/ Principal Secretary, Environment Department periodically review and monitor the progress of implementation of city action plans and State Action Plans under NCAP. The focused actions under NCAP have yielded positive results. During 2025-26, 108 cities recorded reductions in annual PM10 concentrations compared to 2017-18, with 72 cities achieving reductions of more than 20% and 26 cities achieving reductions of more than 40%. Further, 14 cities met the National Ambient Air Quality Standards in FY 2025-26, compared to six cities in 2017-18. Further, during CY 2025, 73 cities recorded reductions in annual PM2.5 concentrations compared to CY 2024, with 17 cities achieving reductions of more than 20%. This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. ***** VM/GS/SK (Rajya Sabha US Q1345) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291891) आगंतुक पटल  : 86 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Compliance by industries प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental clearances in protected areas
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental clearances in protected areas प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has issued Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006 under the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section (2) of Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. As per the provisions laid down in the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, the Projects/ Activities related to Physical Infrastructure including Environmental Services are specified under Item 7 of the Schedule to the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended. Such Projects/Activities are appraised by the Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) at Central Level for Category ‘A’ projects and State Expert Appraisal Committee (SEAC) at the State/UT Level for Category ‘B’ projects, considering all the environmental implications associated with the project. In some cases, certain stretches of infrastructure projects may fall within or adjoining Tiger Reserves or other Protected Areas. Such proposals, once submitted online through the PARIVESH portal are examined on an ongoing basis by this Ministry. Such proposals (involving Tiger Reserves or other Protected Areas) have to undergo a stringent, multi-tier scrutiny and approval process, i.e. one before the EACs for grant of Environmental Clearance (EC) under the EIA Notification, 2006 and second through competent bodies and authorities for seeking Wildlife Clearance under the relevant provisions of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 read with the Ministry’s guidelines and the directions of the Hon’ble Courts. For proper scrutiny and appraisal of projects the Ministry has, on the PARIVESH portal, also developed a Decision Support System (DSS), which is a GIS-enabled spatial visualization and analytical platform that integrates multiple geospatial datasets to assess the environmental sensitivity of project locations. It enables automated proximity analysis of projects with respect to Protected Areas, Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZ), forests, wetlands, coastal regulation zones and other environmentally significant features, thereby providing evidence-based inputs to Expert Appraisal Committees (EACs) and regulatory authorities for informed and expeditious decision-making. Proposals requiring Wildlife Clearance for projects located within Protected Areas or Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZs)/Eco-Sensitive Areas (ESAs) or Forest areas, as applicable, are scrutinised through a multi-tiered mechanism involving the State Chief Wild Life Warden, the State Board for Wild Life, and thereafter the cases so recommended, by the Ministry and the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SCNBWL), which examines the ecological sensitivity of the area, cumulative and specific impacts on wildlife habitats and corridors, and the proposed mitigation measures on a case-to-case basis. The proposals for Wildlife Clearance are recommended by SCNBWL only after due consideration of the impacts, mitigation measures and incorporating appropriate safeguards. Similarly, proposals are granted Environmental Clearance after due consideration of the environmental impacts and incorporation of project-specific environmental safeguards, including mitigation measures prescribed in the Environmental Management Plan (EMP). No construction or other project-related activities can be commenced by the Project Proponents unless prior Wildlife Clearance, as applicable, is obtained under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. During the financial years 2024–25 and 2025–26, a total of 20 infrastructure projects/activities were granted EC following the aforementioned process where the project site is located, wholly or partly, in a Protected Area or Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ)/Eco-Sensitive Area (ESA), as applicable. In accordance with the appraisal carried out by the Expert Appraisal Committee at the Centre/ State/ UT level, as applicable, project-specific environmental safeguards as part of the Environmental Clearance conditions to avoid, minimise and mitigate adverse environmental impacts are prescribed. These include measures relating to wildlife protection, habitat conservation, pollution control, compensatory plantation and environmental monitoring, as applicable. The scientific appraisal process and scrutiny at the approval stage ensures that adequate safeguards are incorporated for the protection of ecologically sensitive landscapes. This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. ***** VM/GS/SK (Rajya Sabha US Q1350) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291889) आगंतुक पटल  : 114 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Environmental clearances in protected areas प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DFS Launches Protection & Indemnity Insurance Product under Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Finance DFS Launches Protection & Indemnity Insurance Product under Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) With the introduction of BMIP, War risk premium rates decrease approximately by 35-40%, from the levels observed at the height of West Asia conflict A total of 1608 Policies covering Cargo and Hull War risks issued under the Pool as on 29th July 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance held an event chaired by Secretary, DFS today in New Delhi to launch India’s first sovereign-backed Protection & Indemnity insurance product under Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP), designed by the New India Assurance Company Limited. The event was attended by Director General of Shipping Shri Shyam Jagannathan, senior officers from Department of Financial Services including Additional Secretary Shri Debasish Prusty, and CMD, General Insurance Corporation of India Shri Hitesh Joshi, CMD, New India Assurance Company Limited, Smt. Girija Subramanian, CMD Shipping Corporation of India Limited Capt. Binesh Kumar Tyagi, Secretary General, General Insurance Council Smt. Kasturi Sengupta, senior officers from ICCSA and INSA and Joint Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Shri Sh. Venkatesapathy S. Speaking on the occasion, Secretary, DFS congratulated all stakeholders involved in the process of formulation of the Protection & Indemnity (P&I) insurance product for achieving this landmark milestone for India’s maritime sector. The Secretary, DFS handed over the first P&I policy document to Shipping Corporation of India Limited issued by the New India Assurance Company Limited under BMIP, providing financial protection against third party liabilities including Crew & Cargo liability, pollution liability, wreck removal, 24x7 port correspondent network with indemnity limit upto USD 1.5 billion, through the combined capacity of the pool. title: Progress under PMKSY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Food Processing Industries Progress under PMKSY PMKSY Strengthens Food Processing Infrastructure, Benefits 37.76 Lakh Farmers and Generates 9.16 Lakh Jobs प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 4:48PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing the Central Sector umbrella scheme Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) across the country. The scheme aims to create modern food processing infrastructure and value addition facilities, enhance processing and preservation of agricultural produce, generate employment opportunities, and provide better remuneration to farmers. As on 30.06.2026, a total of 1,735 projects have been approved under various component schemes of PMKSY, out of which 1,256 projects have been completed, creating 294.21 LMT/Annum of processing and preservation capacity and generating 9.16 lakh employment opportunities across the country. Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY) is demand driven in nature and applications are invited through Expression of Interest (EoI) from all over the country and funds are not allocated/sanctioned/released state-wise under any of the component schemes of PMKSY. The proposals received are scrutinized for their eligibility and evaluated based on the criteria fixed as per the extant scheme guidelines. Merit based approvals are given to the eligible proposals based on availability of funds. As on date, no project has been sanctioned under PMKSY in Bharatpur Parliamentary Constituency. The component schemes under PMKSY provide financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid/subsidy for creation of modern food processing and preservation infrastructure with the objective of reducing post-harvest losses and enhancing value addition. The creation of food processing infrastructure enhances demand for agricultural produce, leading to better price realization and improved income for farmers. PMKSY is a demand driven scheme and applications are invited from all eligible applicants, including Farmers Producing Organisation (FPOs) through Expression of Interest (EoI). To strengthen farmer–producer linkages, PMKSY provides enhanced financial assistance to FPOs along with relaxed eligibility conditions such as lower equity contribution, lower minimum bank loan requirement and a reduced net-worth requirement compared to the general category applicants. Further, Under the centrally sponsored PMFME scheme of the Ministry, FPOs are eligible for a 35% credit-linked subsidy up to ₹10 lakh for setting up or upgrading micro food processing enterprises, 35% grant of up to ₹3 crore for establishing Common Infrastructure and Branding & Marketing support in terms of grant upto 50% for groups of FPOs, at State/regional level. As on 30.06.2026, 1,256 projects have been completed under PMKSY, benefiting about 37.76 lakh farmers and creating 294.21 LMT per annum of processing and preservation capacity, thereby strengthening the food processing ecosystem, promoting value addition, and contributing to the overall exports of food products and growth of the food processing sector. title: Government Boosts Food Processing, Exports and Employment through PLISFPI and PMFME Schemes
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Food Processing Industries Government Boosts Food Processing, Exports and Employment through PLISFPI and PMFME Schemes Performance of the Production Linked Incentive Scheme प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Food Processing Industries is implementing the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) with an approved outlay of ₹10,900 crore for the period from FY 2021-22 to FY 2026-27. The Scheme provides performance-linked incentives on achievement of eligible incremental sales and aims to promote domestic processing and value addition, support creation of global food manufacturing champions, promote Indian food brands in overseas markets and generate employment opportunities. A total of 163 applications from 127 companies, including 69 Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are presently covered under the Scheme. The approved projects are spread across 212 locations in 22 States. Incentives amounting to ₹3,271.44 crore have been disbursed up to June 2026. The Scheme has contributed to expansion of food processing capacity, growth in sales and exports, mobilisation of investment and generation of employment. The investments undertaken under the Scheme have resulted in creation of food processing capacity of 34 lakh metric ton per annum. Approved applicants under PLISFPI have invested ₹9,207 crore against committed investment of ₹7,722 crore and generated approximately 3.35 lakh direct and indirect employment opportunities against the target of 2.50 lakh. Sales of PLI-supported products increased from ₹58,758 crore in FY 2019-20 to ₹1,08,854 crore in FY 2025-26. Details of the units approved under the PLISFPI in aspirational districts are provided in the Annexure. The Ministry implemented the Mega Food Park Scheme, a component scheme under the umbrella scheme Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana since 2008. The Scheme followed a cluster-based hub-and-spoke approach for creation of primary processing, storage, common processing and enabling infrastructure. The Mega Food Park Scheme has been discontinued with effect from 01.04.2021. A total of 41 Mega Food Parks in 25 States have been approved under the Scheme, of which 25 are operational. These projects are expected to create preservation capacity of 28.57 Lakh Metric Ton Per Annum (LMTPA) and processing capacity of 15.41 LMTPA, benefitting approximately 86,881 farmers and generating 1,02,440 direct and indirect employment opportunities. Under PLISFPI, the Government promotes exports and branding of Indian food products abroad through the Branding and Marketing component. Approved applicants are provided financial incentives at the rate of 50 per cent of eligible expenditure incurred on Branding and Marketing Abroad, subject to a maximum of 3 per cent of sales of food products or ₹50 crore per year, whichever is less. The PLISFPI also promotes domestic processing and value addition through performance-linked incentives on eligible incremental sales. The investments undertaken by approved applicants have facilitated expansion of processing capacity and adoption of modern processing, packaging and manufacturing technologies. A separate category has also been provided under the Scheme for Small & Medium Enterprises (SMEs) engaged in innovative and organic food products. The Ministry is also implementing Prime Minister Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) Scheme. PMFME Scheme is a demand driven scheme aimed at providing financial, technical and business support for setting up or upgradation of micro food processing enterprises through capacity building, credit support, technology upgradation and market linkages. The Scheme supports establishment of new enterprises and upgradation of existing enterprises through 35% credit-linked capital subsidy (maximum ₹10 lakh per unit), establishment of Common Infrastructure and Common Incubation Centers (CICs) with modern processing, testing, packaging and storage infrastructure, and provides Branding & Marketing support of up to 50% of the eligible project cost for development of common brands, packaging, labelling and quality standardization. To promote adoption of modern technologies and improve export readiness, the Scheme provides Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDP), product-specific training and technical support through National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM) and State Level Technical Institutions. title: PMKSY Strengthens Food Processing Infrastructure, Reduces Post-Harvest Losses and Boosts Farmers’ Income
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Food Processing Industries PMKSY Strengthens Food Processing Infrastructure, Reduces Post-Harvest Losses and Boosts Farmers’ Income Salient Features of PMKSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 4:45PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) has been implementing a central sector umbrella scheme called “Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY)” since 2017-18 across the country. The salient features of PMKSY are as follows: (i)             Development of integrated food processing and preservation infrastructure across the value chain from farm gate to retail; (ii)            Promotion of value addition and reduction of post-harvest losses; (iii)           Financial assistance for creation/expansion of food processing and preservation capacities; (iv)           Development of integrated cold chain and value addition infrastructure; (v)            Strengthening of food safety and quality assurance infrastructure; (vi)           Promotion of private investment in the food processing sector; (vii)          Generation of employment and enhancement of farmers' income through improved market linkages; and (viii)         Promotion of export competitiveness of processed food products. The objective of PMKSY is to ensure overall development of the food processing sector by incentivizing the creation of modern food processing and preservation infrastructure across the country. The scheme presently comprises six on-going component schemes and two discontinued component schemes (w.e.f. 01.04.2021). The component-wise progress under PMKSY is placed at Annexure I. The State-wise details of projects sanctioned, completed and operational under PMKSY during the last three years along with investment leveraged and employment generated are at Annexure II . The component schemes under PMKSY provide financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid/subsidy for creation of modern food processing and preservation infrastructure with the objective of reducing post-harvest losses and enhancing value addition. The creation of food processing infrastructure enhances demand for agricultural produce, leading to better price realization and improved income for farmers. As on 30.06.2026, 1256 projects are operational under PMKSY, benefiting about 37.76 lakh farmers. PMKSY is a demand-driven scheme and applications are invited from eligible applicants, including Farmers Producer Organisation (FPOs) through Expressions of Interest (EoIs). To strengthen farmer–producer linkages, PMKSY provides enhanced financial assistance to FPOs with loan requirement and a reduced net-worth requirement compared to the general category applicants. Further, under the centrally sponsored PMFME scheme of the Ministry, FPOs are eligible for 35% credit-linked subsidy up to ₹10 lakh for setting up or upgrading micro-food processing enterprises, 35% grant of up to ₹3 crore for establishing Common Infrastructure and Branding & Marketing support in terms of grant upto 50% for groups of FPOs, at State/regional level. The Government regularly monitors the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (PMKSY). As on 30.06.2026, 1735 projects have been approved under PMKSY, of which 1256 projects are operational, creating 294.21 LMT per annum of processing and preservation capacity. The creation of this infrastructure has enhanced value addition, strengthened the food processing ecosystem, improved supply chain efficiency, reduced post-harvest losses through the capacities created under completed projects, and contributed to the growth of the food processing sector and exports of processed food products. Under PMKSY, the Ministry provides financial assistance to eligible applicant organizations/entities/entrepreneurs including rural entrepreneurs for setting up/expansion of eligible projects. PMKSY is a demand-driven scheme. The funds are not allocated/sanctioned/released State-wise under any of the component schemes of PMKSY. Applications are invited through Expressions of Interest (EoIs) from all over India, including aspirational and agricultural regions such as Bundelkhand. The proposals received are scrutinized for eligibility and evaluated as per the applicable scheme guidelines. Financial assistance is provided to eligible projects approved on merit, subject to availability of funds. Through the creation of modern food processing infrastructure, PMKSY promotes value addition of agricultural produce, encourages rural entrepreneurship, generates employment opportunities, and enhances income opportunities for farmers. The creation of this infrastructure has enhanced value addition, strengthened the food processing ecosystem, improved supply chain efficiency, reduced post-harvest losses through the capacities created under completed projects, and contributed to the growth of the food processing sector and exports of processed food products. PMKSY is a demand-driven scheme. The funds are not allocated/sanctioned/released State-wise under any of the component schemes of PMKSY. Applications are invited through Expressions of Interest (EoIs) from all over India, including aspirational and agricultural regions such as Bundelkhand. The proposals received are scrutinized for eligibility and evaluated as per the applicable scheme guidelines. Financial assistance is provided to eligible projects approved on merit, subject to availability of funds. Through the creation of modern food processing infrastructure, PMKSY promotes value addition of agricultural produce, encourages rural entrepreneurship, generates employment opportunities, and enhances income opportunities for farmers. title: IMPLEMENTATION OF RERA ACT, 2016
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs IMPLEMENTATION OF RERA ACT, 2016 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi As per Entry 18 of List- II (State List) of 7 th Schedule of Constitution of India, ‘Land’ and ‘Colonization’ are State subjects. However, by deriving powers from Entries 6, 7 & 46 of List-III (Concurrent List) of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 [RERA] was enacted by the Parliament to regulate the contractual relationship between homebuyers and promoters. RERA aims to ensure transparency & accountability in the Real Estate Sector, thereby protecting the interests of the homebuyers. RERA mandates the registration of real estate projects with the Regulatory Authority before any advertisement, marketing, booking, or sale and in case of contravention of this provision, the promoter is liable to a penalty of up to 10% of the estimated cost of the real estate project, as determined by the Regulatory Authority. Moreover, a Committee was constituted by this Ministry to address challenges during registration of projects across States / Union Territories (UTs) and recommend steps to ensure registration of eligible projects towards effective implementation of RERA. The report of the Committee has been shared with all the Real Estate Regulatory Authorities for further necessary action. RERA also mandates the promoters to disclose all necessary project details & approvals and deposit 70% of the amounts realized from homebuyers in a separate bank account, which shall be utilized only for land cost and project construction. RERA also provides for a fast-track dispute resolution mechanism by making the provision of disposal of matter within 60 days. Section 40 of RERA provides for recovery of unpaid interest, penalty or compensation from the promoter as arrears of land revenue and empowers the Adjudicating Officer, Regulatory Authority or Appellate Tribunal to issue necessary orders or directions. Further, as per Section 41 of RERA, Central Advisory Council (CAC) has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Hon’ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs to advise and recommend the Central Government on all matters concerning the implementation of the Act, including safeguarding the interests of the homebuyers. Moreover, the Ministry regularly communicates with State Governments on various RERA-related issues, including enhancing the functional and administrative autonomy of Regulatory Authorities and ensuring adequate staff deployment as per operational requirements. In last one year, the Ministry has held regular consultations with stakeholders including representatives of Homebuyers’ Associations & Real Estate Developers, State Real Estate Regulatory Authorities, among others, for effective implementation of RERA, development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and amendments needed in the Act. This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ****** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291961) आगंतुक पटल  : 141 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs IMPLEMENTATION OF RERA ACT, 2016 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 6:39PM by PIB Delhi ‘Urban planning’ is a State subject, therefore, the respective State Governments are responsible for planning, initiating and developing proposal for development of urban infrastructure including public transport project, measures to reduce congestion, improve urban mobility through digital technologies etc. in different cities. Central Government has issued various policy guidelines like National Urban Transport Policy 2006 and The Metro Policy 2017 for systematic planning and execution of Public Transport project including metro project, which are applicable to all regions of India. As on date, per se there is no National Smart Public Transport Scheme for integrated public transport, digital ticketing, non- motorized transport, last-mile connectivity. However, Central Government considers Central Financial Assistance, for deployment of e- buses under various Central Schemes (PM e- Bus Sewa, PM e- Drive etc.) and for implementation of Metro projects as and when posed by concerned State Government. Under above interventions digital ticketing, integrated public Transport etc. are priority items. National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) is an interoperable card with vision of “One Nation, One Card”, which works seamlessly among different Metro/RRTS and Bus operators. The Ministry has issued directions for implementation of National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) ecosystem based on qSPARC (quick Specification for Payment Application of RuPay Chip) developed by National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It is functional in 13 Metro projects and 11 Bus Transport corporations by ensuring ease of ticketing through these digital technologies, which facilitates shift from private vehicle to public transport thereby reducing traffic congestion. Further, PM-eBus Sewa Guidelines issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs includes implementation of NCMC based Automatic Fare Collection System (AFCS) for bus operations. Further, under “Transport Planning and Capacity Building in Urban Transport for metro and non metro projects” sub scheme of MoHUA, various studies like preparation of Integrated Mobility Plan, Detailed Project Reports, Multi Modal integration plans etc. have been eligible components for Central Finance Assistance for cities, ULBs etc. which is considered based on feasibility of proposal as and when posed by concerned State Government. This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ****** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291959) आगंतुक पटल  : 84 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs NATIONAL SMART PUBLIC TRANSPORT MISSION प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: UNION MINISTER OF JAL SHAKTI CHAIRS MEETING WITH CHIEF MINISTERS OF CHHATTISGARH AND ODISHA TO FACILITATE AN AMICABLE SETTLEMENT OF THE MAHANADI WATER DISPUTE
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti UNION MINISTER OF JAL SHAKTI CHAIRS MEETING WITH CHIEF MINISTERS OF CHHATTISGARH AND ODISHA TO FACILITATE AN AMICABLE SETTLEMENT OF THE MAHANADI WATER DISPUTE प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C. R. Paatil, today chaired a meeting with Shri Vishnu Deo Sai, Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, and Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Chief Minister of Odisha, to facilitate an amicable settlement of the Mahanadi Water Dispute. Senior officers of the Ministry of Jal Shakti, the Central Water Commission (CWC), and the Governments of both the States also attended the meeting. The meeting marks an important step in the ongoing efforts of the Government of India to facilitate an amicable settlement of the Mahanadi Water Dispute through dialogue, technical cooperation and cooperative federalism. Over the past several years, extensive deliberations and efforts have been made at various levels regarding the sharing of the waters of the Mahanadi. Following the request of the State of Odisha, the Government of India constituted the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal (MWDT) on 12 March 2018 under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956. The Central Government also extended the tenure of the Tribunal to ensure that all parties were provided adequate opportunity to present their views. Recently, the process has gained further momentum with both the States demonstrating their willingness to pursue an amicable settlement through mutual cooperation and technical consultations. The meeting also took note of the progress made by the Joint Technical Committee, which has held number of meetings and achieved consensus on several technical issues. It also noted the constitution of the expanded Technical Committee under chairmanship of Chairman Central Water Commission and comprising representatives of the Governments of Chhattisgarh and Odisha, whose first meeting was held on 29 July 2026 to take forward the remaining technical consultations. Welcoming the Chief Ministers, Shri C. R. Paatil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti observed that the Mahanadi is a lifeline for millions of people in both the States. He emphasized that dialogue, technical cooperation and mutual trust are the most effective means of achieving an equitable, sustainable and mutually acceptable solution. The Union Minister acknowledged the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in bringing states together to resolve long standing water disputes. The Union Minister highlighted that recent milestones, including the signing of the Yamuna Water Project Agreement, the resolution of issues relating to the implementation of the Narmada Water Disputes Tribunal Award, and the consensus on the Modified Parbati–Kalisindh–Chambal (MPKC) Link Project, underscore that even the most complex inter-State water disputes can be resolved through sustained dialogue, cooperative federalism, and consensus-based decision-making. Both the Chief Ministers reaffirmed their commitment to continue the ongoing technical consultations in a constructive spirit and appreciated the facilitation provided by the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the Central Water Commission. Concluding the meeting, Shri C. R. Paatil reiterated that the objective is not merely to resolve the present dispute but to establish a long-term, equitable and sustainable framework for the management of the Mahanadi Basin. He expressed confidence that the continued constructive engagement between the two States would pave the way for a mutually acceptable and enduring settlement. ***** ND/HM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2291997) आगंतुक पटल  : 77 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Jal Shakti UNION MINISTER OF JAL SHAKTI CHAIRS MEETING WITH CHIEF MINISTERS OF CHHATTISGARH AND ODISHA TO FACILITATE AN AMICABLE SETTLEMENT OF THE MAHANADI WATER DISPUTE प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Effectiveness Of Cleanliness and Sanitation Initiatives
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti Effectiveness Of Cleanliness and Sanitation Initiatives SBM(G) Phase-II Accelerates Sustainable Rural Sanitation and ODF Plus Transformation प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 JUL 2026 5:30PM by PIB Delhi Sanitation is State subject. Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase II [SBM(G)-Phase II], is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, implemented by States and Union Territory (UTs) Governments in rural areas within their respective jurisdictions. SBM(G)-Phase II is being implemented in rural areas of the country during the period from 2020-21 to 2026-27, with focus on Open Defecation Free (ODF) sustainability and to cover all the villages with solid and liquid waste management (SLWM) arrangements with visual cleanliness i.e. converting villages from ODF to ODF Plus (Model). The benchmarks for declaration of villages as Open Defecation Free (ODF) Plus under the Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) Phase-II and the categorization are as follows: ODF Plus Aspiring : A village which is sustaining its ODF status and has arrangements for Solid Waste Management OR Liquid Waste Management; ODF Plus Rising : A village which is sustaining its ODF status and has arrangements for both Solid Waste Management and Liquid Waste Management: ODF Plus Model : A village which is sustaining its ODF status and has arrangements for both Solid Waste Management and Liquid Waste Management; observes visual cleanliness, i.e., minimal litter, minimal stagnant wastewater, no plastic waste dump in public places; and displays ODF Plus Information, Education & Communication (IEC) messages. (c) Government of India had launched Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) [SBM(G)], a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, with effect from 2 nd October, 2014 with the aim to attain Open Defecation Free (ODF) India by 2 nd October, 2019 by providing access to toilet facilities in rural areas. More than 10 crore individual household latrines (IHHLs) were constructed under the programme between 2014 to 2019, as per the data reported by the States/UTs. As a result, sanitation coverage in the rural areas of the country has increased from 39% as on 02.10.2014 to 100% and all villages declared themselves ODF in 2019. SBM(G)-Phase-II is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, implemented by States/UTs Governments in rural areas with focus on Open Defecation Free (ODF) sustainability and to cover all the villages with solid and liquid waste management arrangements with visual cleanliness i.e. converting the villages from ODF to ODF Plus (Model). Government of India has been providing financial and technical support to the State/UT Governments to supplement their efforts to improve overall sanitation and SLWM in the rural areas. Besides budgetary support from DDWS (Centre Share) and State share, the States/UTs also converge funds through Finance Commission grants and various Central/State schemes, as per the guidelines, as applicable. Further, under SBM(G) Phase II funds are not released component-wise or project-wise or separately for Aspirational Districts by this Department. However, States/UTs can plan for providing sanitation and hygiene facilities as per the local demand in rural areas, including villages in Aspirational Districts, under their overall AIP. Apart from providing budgetary support, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS) issues operational guidelines, advisories and monitors the implementation of the programme. State/UT-wise Central share of funds released under SBM(G) Phase-II from FY 2020-21 to FY 2025-26 is placed at Annexure .
